article_content: Manchester's legendary Coronation Street set has received official approval to host wedding ceremonies, transforming television history into real-life romance venues. The former ITV production site at Quay Street, operational for 53 years until the show's relocation to MediaCityUK, now permits civil partnerships and non-religious marriages within its iconic Stage One sets. Couples can marry amid replicas of the Rovers Return pub, the Underworld factory, and beloved character homes like the Duckworths' terrace and the Platt family residence. The nearby canal boat from Ken Barlow's storyline remains moored as a photographic backdrop. Managed by Continuum since becoming a visitor attraction in April, the location has already booked corporate events and prepares for its inaugural bar mitzvah next week. With weekday evening rentals starting at £2,500 (accommodating 120 seated guests or 250 reception attendees), interested couples face a deadline - the site closes permanently in October for redevelopment into Manchester's new urban district. Finalized wedding package details are imminent, offering fans a last chance to tie the knot on Weatherfield's cobbles before the set's transformation begins.

article_content: Gabriel Paulista has joined Arsenal's defensive legacy by taking the No. 5 shirt, previously worn by Martin Keown, Steve Bould, and Kolo Touré. The 24-year-old Brazilian completed his £11.2m move from Villarreal on Wednesday after obtaining a work permit through the 'exceptional talent' clause, despite not yet earning senior international caps. Arsenal confirmed on Thursday that Gabriel will fill the number vacated by former captain Thomas Vermaelen, who joined Barcelona in August 2014. The defender, set to earn £60,000 weekly, described his Premier League move as 'a dream come true' and revealed Arsène Wenger personally requested his signing. 'The coach asked for me specifically, which gives me extra motivation,' Gabriel told Arsenal's website. 'His 20-year vision for the club aligns with my ambitions. While we've shown potential, I believe there's significant room for growth to match Arsenal's stature.' Despite Arsenal's inconsistent form this season, Gabriel remains optimistic: 'We must aim for Premier League and Champions League honors consistently. My challenge is to earn playing time alongside Koscielny and Mertesacker, though I'm comfortable across all defensive positions.' The defender acknowledged initial transfer anxieties: 'Adapting to a historic club and iconic stadium excites me. I'm here to contribute collectively, not individually - success comes through team effort.' Gabriel's final Villarreal appearance came before last weekend's La Liga match against Levante, with transfer negotiations already advanced. Reflecting on his journey from Brazil's Esporte Clube Vitória to Spain and now England, he stated: 'Each step fulfilled childhood dreams. My family supported my Premier League ambition, and joining this magnitude of club is incredibly rewarding.'

Vejo potencial, mas acredito que podemos evoluir muito para estar à altura do Arsenal.' Apesar do desempenho irregular do time nesta temporada, Gabriel mantém o otimismo: 'Precisamos brigar por títulos da Premier League e Champions League todo ano. Falando sobre sua trajetória do Vitória da Bahia para a Europa, ele completou: 'Cada passo realizou sonhos. Minha família apoiou meu desejo de jogar na Premier League, e chegar num clube desse tamanho é uma honra.'

article_content: A new wave of cocktail destinations is reviving the golden age of mixology through meticulous recreation of Prohibition-era atmospheres. These establishments blend historical authenticity with modern flair, offering more than just drinks - they deliver time-travel experiences. Boston's perpetually crowded Beehive serves signature champagne cocktails and juleps beneath industrial-chic exposed pipes. Los Angeles' Edison Bar repurposes a power plant's basement into an Art Deco playground, featuring vintage film projections and weekly circus acts. Every Friday from 5-7pm, patrons enjoy 35-cent gin cocktails with grilled cheese during Soup Kitchen Hours. Chicago's Violet Hour enforces digital detox with a strict no-phones policy in velvet-draped parlors using eight specialized ice types. Philadelphia's APO Bar+ Lounge modernizes apothecary traditions through cocktails with ingredients like valerian root, alongside a budget-friendly $6 menu. New York's Flatiron Lounge preserves Jazz Age glamour in its salvaged 1927 mahogany bar, offering martini flights that span cocktail history. Cleveland's measurement-obsessed Velvet Tango Room uses precision scales for $15 cocktails, while Baltimore's Illusions Bar charges $5 weekend covers for magic shows alongside 'magic' martinis. San Francisco's Shanghai 1930 pairs absinthe cocktails with duck lettuce wraps, and New Orleans' rebuilt Sazerac Bar continues its legacy in the Roosevelt Hotel, revived post-Hurricane Katrina in July 2009.
